description_en: Devala Divyapura is a freestanding Shaivaśikharatemple from approx. 8th-10th century.The monument is part of a complex comprising five similar temples distributed accross a longitudinal platform oriented south-north. This platform, also known locally as Dewal Park, is located in the locality of Dewal Divyapur, 3 km west of Chipur and a dozen km north-west of Amargadhi, the district headquarters. The temples were seemingly all dedicated to Shaiva cult, as indicated by the presence ofjalaharīin the sanctums and oneśivaliṅga, placed, in 2014, in the sanctum of Temple 4.Temple 5 is freestanding and lies north of temples 1, 2, 3 and 4. It is oriented to the east. It is composed of a single sanctum (Skt.garbhagṛha). The sanctum is preceded by a short vestibule (Skt.antarāla). This front part is structurally disconnected from the main part of the building. The south, west and north façades of the monument have carved niches blind (Skt.rathikā). There is no image of worship inside the sanctum, but a stonejalaharīis inserted through the north wall. This feature suggests that the temple originally housed aśivaliṅga. The top of theśikharais marked by a largeāmalakaring.The architectural features of the monument evoke temples built in Uttarakhand (India) around the 7th-8th century, and especially Temples 1 and 2 in Jageshwar (seeChanchani 2019, 81-83, fig. 3.7.). It may thus be suggested that this monument, as well as the four others found at the site, was built between the 8th and 10th century (Andolfatto 2022, 38;Sharma 2012, 284). This relative dating places the temples amongst the oldest known form of architecture in west Nepal.
monument_assessment: Heavily damaged (collapsed, demolished, major cracks and structural damages), Demolition/Dismantling, Structural damages
identified_threats: Wall cracks, Erosion, Missing stones at plinths
